name: pw-dependency-skip-cascade
notes: Playwright's dependency-skip cascade must never make a blocked project's tests vanish from the record (spec §11.1 ungameable floor). Run A has setup green: auth-tests executes normally, so both 'auth: always passes' (pass) and the authored 'auth: authored skip' (test.skip(), suppression.marker 'skip') reach onTestEnd and are reported. Run B sets PW_FAIL_SETUP=1: setup fails, auth-tests is entirely blocked, and both tests never reach onTestEnd -- but the recorder still synthesizes them into `observations` as verdict 'skip' with suppression.marker 'dependency' (src/adapters/playwright/recorder.ts toUnreportedObservation). Per the measured constraint in probes/playwright-0b-core/observations/setup-cascade.json, a blocked project's unreported tests (authored skip included) all carry annotations: [] and are structurally indistinguishable, so the authored/dependency distinction can only be asserted on run A's reported record -- run B intentionally asserts both tests converge on marker 'dependency' (regression-fixed, not a bug). At the comparison-report level the comparator itself is unmodified (architecture decision, PR #55 review): the setup regression surfaces as a genuine transitions.new_fail entry (nothing hides the real root cause) and comparability stays 'exact', which is the concrete, mechanical proof that nothing was dropped from B's inventory relative to A -- the dependent tests are not misclassified as transitions.fail_to_skip either (they were never red in the baseline, so that category would be a wrong/gameable attribution). The finer-grained attribution UX (e.g. a dedicated pass-to-skip-via-dependency transition category) is explicitly out of scope per §12-4.
